subject: research/codesign-agri-pulloff
professional: an agricultural robotics / mechanical engineer who designs soft-fruit harvesting end-effectors (strawberry grippers: grip force against bruising, detachment by pulling, bending, twisting or peduncle cutting). They would check first where each force constant comes from and whether it is applied to the same body part and picking motion it was measured for; then whether a friction-hold-against-pull-off model is the right detachment model at all; then whether the optimiser comparison is a research result or a sensitivity sweep of a toy model.

evidence.craft: Read src/codesign_agri_pulloff/pulloff.py (37 lines), tests/test_pulloff.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py, and the parent's agri.py and optimisers.py. Short and readable, seeded, reproducible. Defects: (1) set_grip_bound monkeypatches a private module global of a sibling project (O._UB[3]); it works only because every Pool job re-sets it, and any caller that forgets leaves the parent's optimisers changed process-wide; (2) population() is a copied version of the parent's private _population with one constant changed instead of a parameter on the parent (mitigated by an equality test); (3) sys.path insertion into ../../codesign-agri/src, and pyproject.toml does not declare that dependency; (4) run.py re-filters the 650-record list with nested comprehensions twice and recomputes the medians for the ranking block; no CLI, no output of seed spread (IQR) even though the ranking claims rest on medians differing by 0.001-0.003; (5) results.json carries no metadata (versions, bounds of the design space). No dead code, no silent fallbacks found.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt and my recomputation. Backed: 0.665/0.639/0.502/0.249/0.075 reference J at 8 N; 19% clean, 52% slipped at 13.94 N; -0.033/-0.032/-0.029 medians at 13.94 N; 8 of 10 cells, with the 13.94 N/8 N 'yes' honestly flagged as a ranking among failures; CMA-ES 0.033 < random 0.110 at 10 N/8 N; parent reproduction 0.574/0.611/0.635; 'two fingers low, three or four from 6 N up'. Not backed or stretched: (a) README:13 'the 10 N gripping limit buys 0.03 to 0.04' while the table differences are 0.032, 0.037, 0.026 and 0.045, and my grid puts the 10 N gain at ~0.06 because the 10 N/10 N reference is 0.014 short; (b) project.json:5 says the best design moves 'to four (6 to 13.94 N)', but at 6 N/10 N it has three fingers; (c) README:3 says 'the grip-force limit [is] sourced', but the source (Rajendran et al. 2022, which I fetched and read) gives 10 N as the safe gripping force on the PEDUNCLE (peduncle compression peaks 22.53/26.83 N with safety factor 2), while the model's Fg is total grip force on the FRUIT BODY; the same paper reports Dimeas et al.'s separate 'safe gripping force below 10 N on the fruit body' only for the bend-and-pull technique B, which the README does not cite and which does not apply to the 13.94 N pull-only cells it is paired with; (d) runtime 'about 10 min' not reproduced (22 min here, contended). Disclaimer 'Simulated', AI-assistance note and limitations are present; the second-hand nature of the Dimeas numbers is stated honestly.
evidence.fitness: Research bar (research/CLAUDE.md: PhD-level, aimed at a publishable paper). What a researcher gets: a one-parameter sensitivity sweep of a stylised parent model, showing that when stem pull-off rises past what mu * Fg * cage can supply the achievable objective collapses. That result is close to built into the model: with Fg <= 8 N the hold is at most about 1.34 (mu) x 8 x 1.6 (cage) = 17 N before shear loss, against a 1.1 x fd requirement, so fruit with fd around 13 N cannot be held by construction. The optimiser-ranking part (BO > CMA-ES > random at 40 evaluations) is a property of a 5-D noise-free toy and is not news. Nearest prior work, from recollection plus the two papers I fetched: Dimeas et al. 2015 (gripper design for soft fruit, the source of both pull-off numbers); Rajendran et al. 2022 and the Robofruit system (arXiv:2301.03947), which avoid pull-off by gripping and cutting the peduncle (15 N cut force) and do not touch the flesh; Xiong et al. (2019/2020) strawberry robots that detach by pushing/pulling with a cable-driven gripper; Yamamoto et al. bend detachment; and computational gripper co-design (e.g. Fit2Form, Ha et al. 2020) none of which is discussed. The project does not place its result against any of them, and the one genuinely useful observation (picking motion decides which pull-off value applies) is stated but not modelled. A researcher could reuse the harness, not the conclusion.
evidence.domain: Compared with strawberry end-effector design practice as described in Rajendran et al. 2022 (read: arXiv PDF text, lines on Dimeas technique A 13.94 N / 2.17 mm vs technique B 3.17 N / 1.78 mm, 10 N peduncle gripping limit, 15 N cutting force) and the Robofruit paper. Departures a senior agri-robotics engineer would hit at once: (1) the 10 N peduncle-compression limit is applied as an upper bound on total grip force on the fruit body (pulloff.py:13, run.py:14) - a different organ, different failure mode; (2) detachment is modelled only as friction hold against a straight pull, whereas the cited source's whole point is that end-effectors cut the peduncle (pull-off irrelevant) or bend/twist (3.17 N); pairing the pull-only 13.94 N with any grip bound tests a picking motion practitioners avoid; (3) the two measured values are single means of a single study for different techniques AND different peduncle diameters, but are used as the median of a lognormal with the parent's invented spread 0.3 and ripeness factor (realised median 0.95 x nominal), so the 'measured' cells are not the measurement; 6 N and 10 N are interpolations between two different experiments, not a range of one variable; (4) bruise threshold 40-110 kPa, friction 0.35/0.8 and the caging bonus remain invented, so whether 8 N on a strawberry bruises is not grounded; (5) no fruit mass or acceleration load (the source's own sizing equation Fg = m(g+a)S/mu) in the hold balance. The optimisation method (GP-EI, CMA-ES via the cma package, common random numbers) is standard and correctly run.

defects.what: The sourced '10 N gripping limit' is the safe compression force on the strawberry PEDUNCLE (Rajendran et al. 2022: 22.53/26.83 N peduncle peaks with safety factor 2), but it is used as the upper bound on the model's total grip force on the FRUIT BODY, and the README presents it as a sourced grip-force limit. The only fruit-body 10 N figure in that paper is Dimeas et al.'s, tied to bend-and-pull detachment, which does not apply to the 13.94 N pull-only cells.

The 'reference optimum' (best of five 400-evaluation BO runs) is not the optimum in the 10 N pull-off / 10 N bound cell: an independent brute-force grid reaches J=0.308 vs the reported 0.294, so the claimed gain from the 10 N bound at 10 N pull-off (0.04) is understated (about 0.06), and README's '0.03 to 0.04' range already rounds 0.026 and 0.045 into it.

Detachment is modelled only as friction hold against a straight pull with two single-study means (different technique and peduncle diameter) recast as lognormal medians with the parent's invented spread; peduncle cutting and bend/twist motions, the dominant practice in the cited literature, are absent, and the collapse at 13.94 N follows almost by construction from hold <= ~1.34 x Fg x 1.6. No prior gripper-design or co-design work is placed against the result.

Tests do not cover the experiment path: a seeded change to the ranking predicate in run.py and to the slip safety factor (1.1 -> 1.0) in the parent model both survived; nothing checks any headline number or the reference selection.
project.json summary says the best design moves to four fingers from 6 to 13.94 N; at 6 N with the 10 N bound the reference design has three.

set_grip_bound monkeypatches a private global of the sibling project (O._UB); pyproject does not declare the codesign-agri dependency it reaches through sys.path; ranking claims rest on medians differing by 0.001-0.003 with no spread reported.

verdict: Reproducible and arithmetically right inside its model: run.py regenerated results.txt and results.json byte-for-byte, my own numpy rewrite of the population and score re-derived the printed reference designs' J, outcome fractions and cost, and a brute-force grid confirmed the reference optimum within 0.002 in 9 of 10 cells (it is 0.014 short at 10 N/10 N). It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (2 of 4 seeded mutations survived, including the slip safety factor) and claims is 2, chiefly because the 'sourced' 10 N grip limit is a peduncle-compression limit applied to fruit-body grip force. As research it is a one-parameter sensitivity sweep of an invented toy model whose collapse at high pull-off is close to built in, it models only straight-pull detachment when the cited sources cut or bend the peduncle, and it is not placed against any prior gripper-design work; a senior agricultural-robotics engineer would not sign off the method, and the result is not new.
